subject: echidna
title: Echidnas Can't Sweat or Pant, So They Blow Snot Bubbles

scenes.text: This spiny animal should die on a hot Australian afternoon. It doesn't.
Lab studies said echidnas can't survive above 35 degrees Celsius, 95 Fahrenheit.
They don't sweat, they don't pant, and they don't lick themselves cool.
So in 2023, scientists filmed wild echidnas with heat cameras near Perth.
The trick: they blow snot bubbles. The bubbles pop and wet the tip of the beak.
As it dries, it cools blood flowing through the beak. On camera, the nose was the coldest spot. A runny nose, as air conditioning.

description:
Echidnas can't sweat or pant, yet survive Australian heat above the 35°C (95°F) that lab studies said should kill them.
Using thermal cameras in Western Australia, researchers found echidnas blow snot bubbles that burst and wet the tip of the beak. As the moisture evaporates, it cools a blood-filled sinus there; in infrared, the beak tip was the coolest part of the body. The study was published in Biology Letters in January 2023.
Which animal has the strangest way to stay cool?
first_comment: The researchers say the moist nose also helps echidnas sense electric signals from prey. Which animal has the weirdest cooling trick?
